content.study:
Joint tortfeasors are two or more persons whose conduct makes them jointly responsible for the same tortious injury; in composite negligence, the claimant has not contributed to the accident and may ordinarily recover the whole proved loss from any liable joint tortfeasor, subject to the law governing contribution between the wrongdoers.

Joint liability must be distinguished from contributory negligence. The claimant's own negligence is relevant to contributory negligence; where the claimant is innocent and two or more defendants jointly cause the same damage, the defendants may be jointly and severally liable to the claimant.

This topic is included as a dedicated Torts coverage unit so students can distinguish the doctrine from neighbouring causes of action and apply it to factual problems.

sections.heading: Doctrinal Foundations
sections.body: Joint liability must be distinguished from contributory negligence. The claimant's own negligence is relevant to contributory negligence; where the claimant is innocent and two or more defendants jointly cause the same damage, the defendants may be jointly and severally liable to the claimant.

sections.heading: Essential Elements
sections.body: 1. Two or more persons contribute to the same actionable injury or are jointly responsible for the same tort. 2. The claimant has suffered one indivisible loss attributable to the defendants' conduct. 3. For composite negligence, the claimant did not contribute to the accident. 4. The claimant proves the actionable duty, breach, causation and recoverable damage. 5. Any inter se contribution or apportionment is treated separately from the claimant's right to recover the proved loss.

sections.heading: Application and Boundaries
sections.body: Identify the precise cause of action, establish the required ingredients, distinguish related doctrines, test causation and damage, and then address defences and the appropriate remedy.

sections.heading: Current Verification Status
sections.body: The doctrine and case list require authoritative primary-source judgment verification, citation verification and later-treatment checking before publication.

examples.title: Exam illustration
examples.body: A problem question should identify whether the facts satisfy the elements of Joint Tortfeasors and Composite Negligence, distinguish the nearest alternative doctrine, and conclude only after applying the required ingredients to the proved facts.

examples.title: Boundary illustration
examples.body: Do not treat every procedural error, statutory breach or multi-party accident as automatically establishing the same tort. Identify the precise legal basis of liability.
